network.overall_strategy: This is an evidence-ranked candidate network, not an experimentally validated end-to-end synthesis. Ten graph-distinct pathways are enumerated: six explicitly correlated condition variants of the reported electrical-discharge experiment, one Fischer-Tropsch-type empirical channel, and three speculative sequences using nitrile and carbamoyl masking to reduce amino-aldehyde cyclization. The supplied evidence does not establish ten independent lysine-forming mechanisms. Empirical reactions are lumped feedstock-to-product projections, not resolved elementary mechanisms; their balanceable coproducts do not establish measured lysine-specific fluxes. Conditional routes start from small supplied molecules, including acetaldehyde, acrylonitrile and urea; their environmental availability and concentrations are assumptions, not demonstrated outputs of the cited experiments. Their principal bottlenecks are C5 skeleton construction, selective functionalization, catalyst compatibility and final deprotection. Every numerical condition identified as a screening proposal is unvalidated. Molecular formulas use neutral reference species; actual protonation depends on pH. No oxygen-dependent reaction, enzyme, obligatory cross-environment transfer or enantioselection is assumed. Surface product preservation requires shielding by water, turbidity or rock, not an ozone layer. Null formation environments indicate supplied feedstocks or formation in multiple environments. The strictly anoxic Marshall-to-lysine extrapolation is excluded because the supplied findings do not establish that specific channel.

molecules.common_name: Isocyanic acid; predominantly cyanate at the proposed pH

reactions.name: Buffered electrical discharge with a borosilicate reactor surface
agents: Borosilicate glass: experimentally used surface, not an identified natural mineral equivalent

conditions.temperature: Room temperature, approximately 298 K; exact temperature not specified in the supplied findings
conditions.pressure: Nominal initial dry-gas pressure 0.50 bar, plus water vapor
conditions.catalyst: Borosilicate surface; silanols, adsorption and released trace metals were proposed contributors
conditions.other: Reported nominal gas partial pressures: NH3 0.20 bar, CH4 0.20 bar and N2 0.10 bar. NH4Cl-buffered water at pH 8.7; buffer concentration is not supplied. High-voltage electrical discharge supplies energy. Voltage, current, waveform, electrode gap and exposure duration are not available in the supplied findings and are not invented here. A natural analogue would require a transient reducing gas pocket; its replenishment and photochemical lifetime are unquantified.

reactions.mechanism: Lumped empirical formation of an analyzed product mixture. Radical, cyanide and carbonyl chemistry are possible contributors, but no lysine-specific sequence or nitrogen-source allocation was established.
reactions.reasoning: Criado-Reyes et al. (2021) tentatively assigned lysine in this condition at approximately 10.86 micrograms per milligram of crude product. This is not a feedstock conversion yield or an independently confirmed free-lysine production rate. Glass enhanced the overall network, but equivalence to a natural silicate interface is unproven. H2 is a formal balance-enabling coproduct, not a measured lysine-specific flux; listing both nitrogen feeds does not establish their incorporation. Confirmation requires authentic standards, orthogonal analysis and isotope tracing.

reactions.name: Buffered electrical discharge without added silicate

conditions.pressure: Nominal initial dry-gas pressure 0.50 bar, plus water vapor
conditions.other: Teflon reactor; no added silicate. Nominal initial partial pressures: NH3 0.20 bar, CH4 0.20 bar, N2 0.10 bar. NH4Cl-buffered water at pH 8.7. High-voltage discharge; electrical settings, duration, electrode composition and buffer concentration are not specified in the supplied findings. Null catalyst means no intentionally added catalyst, not demonstrated absence of electrode or impurity effects.

reactions.mechanism: Unresolved electrical-discharge reaction network producing a mixture with a tentative lysine assignment.
reactions.reasoning: Criado-Reyes et al. (2021) reported approximately 2.88 micrograms of assigned lysine per milligram of crude product in buffered Teflon. This supports an added-silicate-independent empirical channel, not a catalyst-free elementary mechanism. The identification, nitrogen-source allocation and H2 coproduct caveats of rxn_001 also apply. This is a condition variant of the same experimental family, not independent mechanistic evidence.

reactions.name: Buffered electrical discharge with dispersed borosilicate pieces

conditions.pressure: Nominal initial dry-gas pressure 0.50 bar, plus water vapor
conditions.catalyst: Dispersed borosilicate surface; lysine-specific catalytic action unresolved
conditions.other: Teflon vessel containing borosilicate pieces. NH3 0.20 bar, CH4 0.20 bar and N2 0.10 bar nominal initial partial pressures. NH4Cl-buffered aqueous phase at pH 8.7. High-voltage discharge. Glass surface area, dissolution rate, buffer concentration and electrical dose are not available in the supplied findings.

reactions.mechanism: Lumped discharge chemistry with adsorption and surface-mediated changes to the broader reaction mixture.
reactions.reasoning: Criado-Reyes et al. (2021) tentatively assigned approximately 2.39 micrograms of lysine per milligram of crude product. This value does not demonstrate that dispersed glass specifically improves lysine production relative to the buffered Teflon condition. Natural mineral equivalence, target identity and actual coproduct fluxes remain unresolved. This is another condition variant, not a separate established chemical mechanism.

reactions.name: Unbuffered alkaline electrical discharge with a borosilicate reactor surface

conditions.pressure: Nominal initial dry-gas pressure 0.50 bar, plus water vapor
conditions.catalyst: Borosilicate surface and potentially released trace constituents
conditions.other: Unbuffered aqueous phase at approximately pH 11. Nominal initial partial pressures: NH3 0.20 bar, CH4 0.20 bar, N2 0.10 bar. High-voltage electrical discharge. Dissolved ammonia concentration after equilibration, pH history, electrical dose and glass dissolution history are not provided. Sustained natural ammonia abundance under strong UV is not assumed.

reactions.mechanism: Unresolved coupled discharge and alkaline surface chemistry; HCN-rich films and other mixed products can accumulate.
reactions.reasoning: Criado-Reyes et al. (2021) reported approximately 30.71 micrograms of tentatively assigned lysine per milligram of crude product. The comparatively large crude-product abundance does not resolve identification uncertainty or establish feedstock efficiency. Alkaline glass alteration complicates extrapolation to natural surfaces. This shares the analytical limitations and unmeasured lysine-specific H2 flux of the other discharge variants.

reactions.name: Unbuffered alkaline electrical discharge without added silicate

conditions.pressure: Nominal initial dry-gas pressure 0.50 bar, plus water vapor
conditions.other: Teflon vessel with no added silicate. Unbuffered water at approximately pH 11. Nominal initial partial pressures: NH3 0.20 bar, CH4 0.20 bar, N2 0.10 bar. High-voltage discharge; quantitative electrical settings and treatment duration are not supplied. A local reducing atmosphere is a boundary condition, not a demonstrated geological gas source.

reactions.mechanism: Empirical mixture-level electrical-discharge formation; individual carbon-chain-growth and nitrogen-incorporation steps are unresolved.
reactions.reasoning: Criado-Reyes et al. (2021) tentatively assigned approximately 12.33 micrograms of lysine per milligram of crude product. This again shows that added borosilicate was not obligatory for the reported assignment. It does not demonstrate immunity to vessel, electrode or trace-metal effects, nor an environmentally sustained NH3-rich atmosphere. This is a correlated condition variant.

reactions.name: Unbuffered alkaline electrical discharge with dispersed borosilicate pieces

conditions.pressure: Nominal initial dry-gas pressure 0.50 bar, plus water vapor
conditions.other: Teflon reactor containing glass pieces; unbuffered aqueous phase at approximately pH 11. NH3 0.20 bar, CH4 0.20 bar and N2 0.10 bar nominal initial partial pressures. High-voltage discharge. Particle surface area, electrical dose, residence time and natural glass-equivalent composition are unresolved in the supplied findings.

reactions.mechanism: Lumped discharge chemistry modified by an evolving alkaline glass-water interface.
reactions.reasoning: Criado-Reyes et al. (2021) tentatively assigned approximately 15.17 micrograms of lysine per milligram of crude product. This is experimental support for the stated laboratory condition, not proof of an independent lysine mechanism or of a corresponding natural mineral assemblage. Target confirmation and actual coproduct accounting remain necessary.

reactions.name: Fischer-Tropsch-type lysine-containing product formation and cooled recovery
agents: Nickel metal; geological availability of a comparably active surface is conditional

conditions.temperature: 473-600 K proposed hydrothermal-fracture screening window; the cited experimental family spans 473-973 K
conditions.pressure: 1-5 MPa proposed gas-rich fracture conditions; the original experimental pressure is not given in the supplied findings
conditions.catalyst: Exposed nickel metal, not an assumed generic iron-sulfide catalyst
conditions.other: The proposed reaction zone is gas-solid, not hot aqueous solution. It requires connected gas-filled pores, sufficient CO and H2 fugacity, removal of generated water, and nickel not passivated by sulfide or oxide. The supplied findings do not identify a lysine-positive operating point within 473-600 K or provide a validated residence time. Residence time must be screened against destruction. Recovery requires cooling below approximately 330 K before aqueous collection; quench rate and extraction efficiency are design requirements, not measured geological performance.

reactions.mechanism: Lumped empirical heterogeneous synthesis and recovery. CO activation, reduction, chain growth and nitrogen incorporation are plausible reaction families, but no discrete lysine-specific intermediate sequence was established.
reactions.reasoning: Yoshino, Hayatsu and Anders (1971) reported lysine among products from CO/H2/NH3 over heterogeneous catalysts, with total amino-acid yields no greater than approximately 0.1%. Hayatsu, Studier and Anders (1971) supplied isotope-supported confirmation in related experiments. That evidence supports the experimental family, not every catalyst-temperature-pressure combination proposed here. The restricted hydrothermal implementation remains conditional. Gas-solid results cannot be transferred directly to aqueous vents, and free lysine before work-up must not be assumed. Bada, Miller and Zhao (1995) and Aubrey, Cleaves and Bada (2009) motivate explicit preservation tests rather than an equilibrium-based accumulation claim.

reactions.name: Candidate C5 construction by acetaldehyde conjugate addition to acrylonitrile
agents: Hydroxide supplied by alkaline water: proposed general-base catalyst

conditions.catalyst: General-base catalysis by alkaline water; productive catalysis is unvalidated
conditions.other: Proposed screen: pH 9.5-11, acetaldehyde 10-100 mM, acrylonitrile 1-10 mM, hours to days. These concentrations and times are not literature-established lysine conditions. Ammonia and cyanide are introduced only after this stage to avoid additional addition reactions. Acetaldehyde volatilization, self-aldol chemistry, acrylonitrile polymerization and product overreaction must be quantified.

reactions.mechanism: A small acetaldehyde enolate population could add at the beta carbon of acrylonitrile, followed by protonation to give OHC-(CH2)3-CN.
reactions.reasoning: Speculative: no study in the supplied findings demonstrates this prebiotic C5 construction. It is included because its carbon connectivity is correct and it keeps the future epsilon nitrogen masked as a nitrile instead of generating a rapidly cyclizing amino aldehyde. Weak aqueous enolization and competing oligomerization may prevent useful flux entirely. McDonald and Storrie-Lombardi (2010) contextualize the unresolved precursor problem; their review is not evidence that this particular reaction works.

reactions.name: Strecker conversion of the nitrile-masked C5 aldehyde

conditions.other: Proposed screen: pH 8-9, aldehyde 1-10 mM, total ammonia/ammonium 50-200 mM and total HCN/cyanide 5-30 mM, monitored over hours to days. A covered or shaded aqueous compartment limits volatile loss and photolysis. The alpha-amino product must be captured or protonated before prolonged storage. No experimentally established yield or lifetime is available.

reactions.mechanism: Aldehyde-ammonia condensation followed by cyanide addition installs the alpha-amino group and the future carboxyl carbon while retaining the terminal nitrile.
reactions.reasoning: Speculative for this substrate. Criado-Reyes et al. (2021) discuss Strecker chemistry in their overall mixture, but do not establish this dinitrile intermediate. Retaining a terminal nitrile avoids the especially reactive omega-amino aldehyde, but does not eliminate intramolecular chemistry: the new alpha amine could attack the distal nitrile to form a cyclic amidine under activating conditions. Product identification, capture kinetics and competing pathways must therefore be measured.

reactions.name: Carbonate-mediated hydantoin capture of the masked aminonitrile
agents: Dissolved bicarbonate/carbonate as the reactive form of the carbon dioxide feed

conditions.other: Proposed screen: pH 8-9.5, total inorganic carbon 0.05-0.5 M and ammonia/ammonium 0.05-0.2 M. CO2 is represented by its neutral reference formula but is mainly bicarbonate/carbonate here. Monitor aminonitrile disappearance and hydantoin identity over hours to days. Carbonate is a consumed reagent, not an assumed catalytic mineral.

reactions.mechanism: Bucherer-Bergs-type carbamylation and cyclization convert the alpha-aminonitrile into a hydantoin while retaining the side-chain nitrile.
reactions.reasoning: Speculative substrate-specific application of recognizable hydantoin chemistry. Criado-Reyes et al. (2021) discuss Bucherer-Bergs-type reactions, but do not demonstrate this intermediate or these operating conditions. Hydantoin formation could mask the alpha nitrogen before terminal nitrile reduction, addressing a concrete cyclization risk. It does not establish rxn_008 or guarantee that capture outruns cyclic amidine formation.

reactions.name: Terminal nitrile hydrogenation with the alpha functionality retained in a hydantoin

conditions.pressure: 2-10 MPa total, with 1-5 MPa H2 partial pressure proposed
conditions.catalyst: Nickel metal; activity of a geological surface must be established
conditions.other: Proposed pH 8-10 and ammonia/ammonium 0.05-0.5 M to test suppression of secondary-amine formation. Suggested residence-time screen: 0.5-24 h, not a validated synthesis interval. Cyanide and CO carryover must be measured because they can inhibit nickel. A separate low-sulfide reducing compartment is required; compatible transfer has not been demonstrated. Cool recovered products below approximately 330 K.

reactions.mechanism: Surface hydrogenation of the terminal nitrile through imine-like intermediates installs the epsilon-amino group while the alpha nitrogen remains masked.
reactions.reasoning: Speculative geochemical application of metal-catalyzed nitrile hydrogenation. Kaur et al. (2024) establish Ni/H2-driven reductive amination of other substrates, not this nitrile reduction or lysine synthesis. Masking the alpha nitrogen reduces interception of the terminal imine by a free alpha amine. Selectivity against ring-carbonyl reduction, secondary amines and hydantoin degradation remains unmeasured. Proposed H2 pressures are screening assumptions, not demonstrated vent inventories.

reactions.name: Ring opening of lysine hydantoin to N-alpha-carbamoyllysine

conditions.pressure: 1-5 MPa, maintaining a liquid aqueous phase
conditions.other: Proposed pH 10-11.5 with a 1-48 h analytical screening interval. Hydantoin ring-opening regioselectivity must be measured; the desired product is the N-alpha-carbamoyl amino acid. Ring reclosure, side-chain acylation and decomposition are possible. No usable yield or residence time is established.

reactions.mechanism: Hydrolytic opening of the hydantoin acyl-nitrogen bond produces an N-carbamoyl amino acid without yet releasing the alpha amine.
reactions.reasoning: Speculative for this substrate and geochemical window. The hydantoin reaction class discussed by Criado-Reyes et al. (2021) does not validate selective ring opening of lysine hydantoin. Aubrey, Cleaves and Bada (2009) show why extended heating cannot be assumed compatible with amino-acid accumulation. The epsilon amine can introduce additional acyl-transfer chemistry, so product analysis must distinguish the desired open-chain compound from cyclic products.

reactions.name: Hydantoin ring opening before terminal nitrile reduction

conditions.other: Proposed pH 10-11 and 1-24 h screening. The required selectivity is hydantoin ring opening while retaining both the terminal nitrile and the alpha carbamoyl group. Sample frequently and cool aliquots immediately. No substrate-specific kinetic separation between these hydrolyses is known from the supplied findings.

reactions.mechanism: Selective ring hydrolysis produces an open-chain N-carbamoyl amino acid whose terminal nitrogen remains a nitrile.
reactions.reasoning: Speculative ordering alternative, not independent experimental evidence. It differs chemically from rxn_011 followed by rxn_012 because the hydrogenation substrate becomes an open-chain carboxylate rather than a hydantoin. The alpha nitrogen remains masked, unlike routes that expose an amino aldehyde before reduction. Neither Criado-Reyes et al. (2021) nor the hydrothermal studies establish the required selectivity; preservation constraints from Aubrey, Cleaves and Bada (2009) remain relevant.

reactions.name: Terminal nitrile hydrogenation of the open-chain N-carbamoyl precursor

conditions.pressure: 2-10 MPa total; proposed H2 partial pressure 1-5 MPa
conditions.other: Proposed pH 8-10, ammonia/ammonium 0.05-0.5 M and 0.5-24 h screening. The acid is predominantly carboxylate. Residual free cyanide, cyanate and sulfur compounds must be assayed for catalyst effects. Retention of the carbamoyl group and suppression of secondary-amine formation must be established before claiming productive flux.

reactions.mechanism: Hydrogenation converts the terminal nitrile to a primary amine while retaining the alpha-N-carbamoyl protecting functionality.
reactions.reasoning: Speculative substrate-specific nitrile hydrogenation. Kaur et al. (2024) support the broader plausibility of Ni-mediated H2 activation under aqueous prebiotic conditions, but do not demonstrate this reaction. The masked alpha nitrogen should be less nucleophilic than a free alpha amine, reducing one route to cyclic imine-derived products. Carboxylate adsorption, catalyst poisoning and deprotection during hydrogenation remain unresolved.

reactions.name: Hydrolytic removal of the alpha-carbamoyl group to release lysine

conditions.other: Proposed pH 1-2 in a separate acidic compartment, with a 0.5-24 h screening interval. Both lysine amino groups are predominantly protonated. NH3 and CO2 in the graph represent the corresponding pH-dependent dissolved species and gas. Acidification, residence time and cooling below approximately 330 K must be validated together. No selective environmental transfer or lysine recovery efficiency is assumed.

reactions.mechanism: Hydrolysis of the substituted urea functionality releases the alpha amine; the carbamoyl carbon and nitrogen leave as inorganic carbon and ammonia/ammonium.
reactions.reasoning: Speculative final deprotection; no supplied study demonstrates a useful lysine yield from this precursor under these conditions. Carbamoyl groups can require appreciable activation, and hydantoin reformation can compete. This is a major bottleneck rather than an automatic final step. Bada, Miller and Zhao (1995) and Aubrey, Cleaves and Bada (2009) establish the need to compare deprotection rates with amino-acid destruction. Product identity, carbon recovery and free-lysine survival must all be measured.

reactions.name: Selective alpha-aminonitrile hydrolysis while retaining the distal nitrile

conditions.other: Proposed pH 1-2 and 1-72 h screening. Protonation suppresses nucleophilicity of the alpha amine. The desired endpoint requires hydrolysis of the alpha-aminonitrile-derived group without substantial hydrolysis of the terminal nitrile. No experimentally demonstrated selectivity window is supplied.

reactions.mechanism: Hydration and hydrolysis of the alpha nitrile produce the carboxylic acid through an amide intermediate; the distal nitrile must remain intact.
reactions.reasoning: Speculative selective application of ordinary nitrile hydrolysis. The supplied literature supports the general Strecker endpoint but not discrimination between these two nitriles. Different electronic environments make differential rates conceivable, not established. Distal nitrile hydrolysis, cyclic amidine chemistry and incomplete conversion could eliminate useful yield. This branch is retained only as a testable alternative to hydantoin capture, not as a demonstrated solution to the precursor problem discussed by McDonald and Storrie-Lombardi (2010).

reactions.name: Cyanate-mediated alpha-amino carbamoylation

conditions.other: Proposed pH 7.5-9 after cooling and partial neutralization of the preceding acidic hydrolysate. Cyanate is the dominant inorganic species; reactive isocyanic acid is a minor equilibrium component. Proposed amino-acid concentration 1-10 mM with cyanate delivered from rxn_018 and measured rather than assumed. Monitor carbamoylation against cyanate hydrolysis and cyclization.

reactions.mechanism: The alpha amine captures isocyanic acid from the cyanate equilibrium, producing an N-carbamoyl amino acid before the terminal nitrile is reduced.
reactions.reasoning: Speculative prebiotic implementation with no direct support for this substrate in the supplied studies. Amine carbamoylation is chemically recognizable and provides a specific masking function rather than adding an arbitrary intermediate. Success requires adequate cyanate supply, sufficient unprotonated amine and retention of the distal nitrile. This route does not inherit experimental validation merely because carbamoylated amino acids are chemically accessible.

reactions.name: Conditional cyanate supply from aqueous urea

conditions.other: Proposed concentrated urea pool, 0.05-0.5 M, pH 8-9.5, monitored over hours to days. Urea, ammonium and cyanate interconvert; substantial cyanate accumulation must not be presumed. Volatile loss, cyanate hydrolysis and competition from ammonia must be measured. Neutral HNCO and NH3 formulas represent acid-base-equilibrated products.

reactions.mechanism: Reversible urea dissociation supplies a potentially small ammonium-cyanate pool; consumption by rxn_017 could trap part of that pool.
reactions.reasoning: Speculative environmental supply module. Urea-cyanate interconversion is established reaction-class chemistry, but the supplied research does not demonstrate a concentrated prebiotic urea reservoir or adequate cyanate flux for this network. This step is necessary only for P10 and is not credited as an independent lysine synthesis. Low cyanate availability or competing hydrolysis would invalidate that branch.

pathways.name: Buffered borosilicate discharge channel
pathways.description: Reported laboratory condition with tentative lysine identification. A condition variant of the discharge family, not an independently resolved chemical mechanism.

pathways.name: Buffered discharge without added silicate
pathways.description: Reported Teflon condition showing that added silicate was not obligatory for the tentative assignment. Electrode and trace-material effects remain possible.

pathways.name: Buffered discharge with dispersed glass
pathways.description: Reported buffered glass-particle condition. Graph-distinct from P1 and P2 but analytically and mechanistically correlated with them.

pathways.name: Unbuffered alkaline borosilicate discharge channel
pathways.description: Reported condition with the largest assigned lysine abundance per mass of crude product in the supplied discharge data. This does not establish the highest feedstock yield or strongest identification.

pathways.name: Unbuffered alkaline discharge without added silicate
pathways.description: Reported Teflon condition at approximately pH 11. Its environmental gas inventory and tentative target assignment remain unresolved.

pathways.name: Unbuffered alkaline discharge with dispersed glass
pathways.description: Reported unbuffered glass-particle condition. This completes six experimentally differentiated discharge channels, not six independent mechanisms.

pathways.name: Heterogeneous CO/H2/NH3 synthesis with cooled recovery
pathways.description: The strongest historical isotope-supported experimental family in the supplied evidence. Its proposed 473-600 K high-pressure gas-solid implementation, residence time and lysine recovery remain unvalidated.

pathways.name: Masked-nitrile Strecker route with hydrogenation before hydantoin opening
pathways.description: Conditional route from acetaldehyde and acrylonitrile through a C5 nitrile-aldehyde, aminodinitrile and hydantoin. The terminal nitrile is reduced while the alpha nitrogen is masked; subsequent ring opening and deprotection release lysine. No integrated step sequence has been demonstrated. C5 construction, hydantoin capture and deprotection are major bottlenecks.

pathways.name: Masked-nitrile Strecker route with hydantoin opening before hydrogenation
pathways.description: Conditional ordering alternative to P8. Selective hydantoin opening gives an open-chain N-carbamoyl substrate for terminal nitrile reduction. The alpha nitrogen remains masked throughout reduction. This changes substrate chemistry but supplies no independent experimental validation and adds a hydrolysis-selectivity requirement.

pathways.name: Selective aminonitrile hydrolysis followed by cyanate masking and terminal reduction
pathways.description: Conditional route that bypasses hydantoin formation. A parallel urea branch supplies cyanate. Selective alpha-nitrile hydrolysis is followed by alpha-amino carbamoylation, terminal nitrile reduction and final deprotection. The reaction sequence is a dependency order including the separate cyanate supply branch. Selective hydrolysis and sufficient cyanate flux are additional unvalidated requirements.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This is a defensible empirical input-output channel corresponding to Criado-Reyes et al. (2021), rather than an established elementary reaction. The supplied balance check establishes conservation, but not the inferred hydrogen coproduct flux or nitrogen-source allocation. Lysine identification remains tentative GC-MS evidence. Buffered discharge is compatible with a surface setting, although the reaction entry does not specify the operational conditions or establish equivalence between laboratory borosilicate and a natural surface.
suggestions: Attach the source citation and specify buffer composition, pH, gas partial pressures, temperature, discharge conditions and reaction duration.
Confirm lysine with authentic standards, orthogonal chromatography/mass spectrometry and labeled carbon and nitrogen feedstocks.
If claiming natural environmental applicability, test the relevant natural glass or silicate rather than assuming equivalence to laboratory borosilicate.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The no-added-silicate condition is supported by the buffered control in Criado-Reyes et al. (2021). Its empirical status is comparable to P1: reported lysine assignment, but no resolved lysine-specific mechanism or isotope-traced synthesis. Absence of added silicate does not establish absence of electrode, vessel or trace-metal effects. The network appropriately identifies this as a correlated condition variant rather than an independent mechanism.
suggestions: Preserve the tentative-identification qualification and add a reaction-level citation.
Specify the published buffered conditions and characterize electrode, vessel and trace-metal contributions.
Measure confirmed lysine production relative to feedstock consumption, not only its abundance within crude product.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This matches the buffered dispersed-borosilicate condition reported by Criado-Reyes et al. (2021). It supports an empirical lysine-assigned product channel, but neither a distinct formation mechanism nor a demonstrated lysine-specific catalytic role for glass. Conservation is satisfied. Environmental extrapolation requires characterization of the glass loading, dissolution products and solution conditions, while target confidence remains limited by the tentative analytical assignment.
suggestions: Specify glass composition, loading, surface area, buffer conditions and dissolved-metal concentrations.
Use isotope-resolved product confirmation and replicate the dispersed-glass control.
Separate changes in total organic production from changes in absolute lysine production and recovery.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The unbuffered alkaline borosilicate experiment in Criado-Reyes et al. (2021) provides direct, although tentative, product-assignment evidence. Its comparatively high reported lysine abundance per mass of crude product is not a feedstock conversion yield and does not independently resolve identity or mechanism. An alkaline, electrically energized surface setting is chemically compatible, but maintaining the gas mixture and pH requires an explicit local scenario.
suggestions: Specify initial and time-dependent pH, gas replenishment, discharge exposure and product collection conditions.
Report absolute confirmed lysine production and carbon/nitrogen recovery alongside crude-product composition.
Test product survival during continued discharge and subsequent collection.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Criado-Reyes et al. (2021) reported a lysine assignment in the corresponding unbuffered no-added-silicate experiment. This supports treating added borosilicate as non-obligatory for the reported channel, without establishing that all heterogeneous influences are absent. The reaction is conservation-compatible as an empirical projection. Target identification, operating conditions and the environmental persistence of the reducing gas mixture remain unresolved.
suggestions: Confirm the assigned lysine using authentic standards and isotope-labeled feedstocks.
Document electrode and vessel controls together with gas composition and pH evolution.
Specify a physically justified local reducing setting without assuming a globally persistent laboratory-like atmosphere.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This corresponds to the unbuffered dispersed-glass condition in Criado-Reyes et al. (2021). The experimental correspondence supports a tentative empirical channel, not a resolved lysine synthesis sequence. The network correctly treats this evidence as correlated with the other discharge conditions. Glass-associated changes in adsorption, dissolution and product recovery should be distinguished from a demonstrated increase in lysine-specific formation flux.
suggestions: Specify glass loading, composition, pH history and discharge conditions with a reaction-level citation.
Measure lysine in both solution and surface-associated material using recovery controls.
Confirm product identity independently before interpreting differences between discharge conditions mechanistically.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This has the strongest direct lysine-formation evidence in the supplied research: Yoshino, Hayatsu and Anders (1971), strengthened by the isotope-based experiments of Hayatsu, Studier and Anders (1971). A lumped empirical edge is appropriate, and the inferred stoichiometry is balanced. However, the historical 200-700 °C heterogeneous experiments do not establish an equivalent bulk-aqueous hydrothermal reaction. Cooled recovery addresses preservation conceptually, but catalyst identity, phase, pressure, residence time and recovery procedure remain unspecified. Low aggregate amino-acid yields do not establish a lysine-specific yield.
suggestions: Select a documented lysine-positive experimental condition and specify its catalyst, temperature, pressure, gas composition and residence time.
Distinguish the hot heterogeneous reaction zone from aqueous collection, and quantify cooling and product survival.
State whether lysine is recovered directly or appears after additional workup; include any required workup explicitly.
Measure lysine-specific yield and recovery rather than assigning the total amino-acid yield to lysine.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The carbon connectivity is correct: conjugate addition can formally furnish 4-cyanobutanal, Strecker chemistry adds the carboxyl carbon precursor, and terminal nitrile reduction supplies the lysine epsilon-amino group. Hydantoin masking rationally avoids requiring accumulated 5-aminopentanal. Nevertheless, rxn_008 lacks demonstrated selectivity against acetaldehyde aldol chemistry, repeated addition and acrylonitrile polymerization. Strecker and Bucherer-Bergs precedents do not validate this exact sequence. No active hydrogenation catalyst is specified for rxn_011, and rxn_015 requires demonstrated carbamoyl cleavage without excessive degradation. As labeled, mol_015 must move between settings or experience a justified local condition change.
suggestions: Demonstrate rxn_008 with quantified selectivity, substrate concentrations and competing products before relying on downstream transformations.
Verify masked aminonitrile and hydantoin identities and yields under explicit ammonia, cyanide and carbonate conditions.
Identify an environmentally justified hydrogenation catalyst and measure terminal-nitrile conversion, hydantoin survival and inhibition by any carried-over cyanide.
Measure ring-opening and decarbamoylation kinetics against lysine degradation, and specify transport or local heating conditions for mol_015.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This is a structurally coherent alternative to P8, and all reactions pass the supplied conservation check. Opening the hydantoin before hydrogenation avoids requiring its survival during reduction, but introduces a different unvalidated selectivity requirement: rxn_013 must open the ring while retaining the distal nitrile. The resulting carboxylate and carbamoyl functionality may also affect catalyst activity in rxn_014. The shared C5-construction and final decarbamoylation bottlenecks remain. The supplied literature does not demonstrate this substrate-specific sequence, and the Surface-to-Hydrothermal assignment lacks a physical implementation.
suggestions: Determine a kinetic window for hydantoin opening that retains the terminal nitrile rather than hydrolyzing it to an amide or carboxylate.
Test hydrogenation of the actual open-chain N-carbamoyl substrate with a specified catalyst, hydrogen pressure and solution composition.
Demonstrate final lysine release and survival instead of assuming that hydrothermal heating removes the carbamoyl group selectively.
Specify how mol_015 reaches the required hydrolysis setting, including dilution, residence time and intermediate stability.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: The proposed intermediate identities and final lysine connectivity are consistent. Cyanate-mediated amino-group carbamoylation is credible reaction-class chemistry, and aqueous urea can supply cyanate through a condition-dependent equilibrium. However, rxn_016 requires experimentally unestablished discrimination between two nitriles; hydrolysis of the distal nitrile would remove the intended route to the epsilon-amino group. Rxn_018 does not establish an adequate cyanate supply rate, especially without concentrations, pH and time. Selective hydrogenation and final decarbamoylation remain unresolved. Mol_018 also crosses the stated environment labels without a specified transfer or local condition-change scenario.
suggestions: Measure site-selective nitrile hydrolysis directly, identifying both desired and distal-hydrolysis products over time.
Quantify cyanate production from urea and its capture by mol_017 under explicit pH, temperature, ammonia and concentration conditions.
Determine whether carbamoylation outcompetes cyanate loss and other reactions in the actual precursor mixture.
Validate terminal-nitrile hydrogenation and final deprotection with authentic intermediates, and specify the environmental handoff for mol_018.

evaluation.network_feedback: The network has strong formal validity: the molecule and reaction nodes are connected, IDs are used consistently, and the proposed intermediates have the correct carbon connectivity for lysine. The deterministic check establishes that all 18 reactions conserve atoms and charge with appropriate coefficients; none is an identified conservation violation. The inferred empirical stoichiometries are not evidence of measured lysine-specific fluxes. Literature alignment is strongest for P7 and qualified for P1-P6, whose lysine assignments remain tentative. The six discharge conditions are appropriately treated as correlated evidence, not six independent confirmations. The proposal also correctly distinguishes speculative chemistry from reported empirical channels and avoids the unsupported anoxic Marshall extrapolation. P8-P10 provide chemically intelligible masking strategies, but their C5 construction, chemoselective transformations, catalyst compatibility and final carbamoyl removal are not demonstrated under specified conditions. Their weakness is not their length, hub structure or use of multiple environments. As labeled, they require an explicit physical account of transport or changing local conditions; the statement that no obligatory transfer is assumed does not supply that account. Reaction-level citations and operational conditions are missing throughout, although the supplied research provides context for the empirical channels. The declared starting molecules are legitimate conditional inputs, but their local concentrations and compatibility remain assumptions. Overall, the network supports experimentally motivated candidate routes, including a comparatively strong empirical lysine-forming channel, but not a validated environmentally coherent complete synthesis network. It does not meet the 0.90 network-approval threshold.
